Feature-gated AllocStats/stats_alloc behind a mem-trace Cargo feature in both crates. Since diplomat-tool/the jolt backend parse lib.rs textually (no cfg evaluation), bind.clj now supports --features/--out-suffix to produce two fully separate trees per crate: default (generated/, target/, consumable, no AllocStats symbols) and traced (generated-traced/, target-traced/ via CARGO_TARGET_DIR, --features mem-trace, AllocStats present). New examples/{base64,json}/leak-check/ subprojects load the traced dylib+shim directly and exercise leak_check.clj/leak_check_neg.clj against it. Verified: demo.clj unaffected on default build; leak-check numbers unchanged from pre-retrofit (base64 0 leaked / 323 bytes-per-iter negative control, json 0 leaked / 32 bytes-per-iter negative control).

Instrumented chrono per the verified pattern: mem-trace feature gate added correctly from the start (no retrofit needed), AllocStats opaque, two-tree bind.clj (generated/ consumable + generated-traced/), examples/chrono/leak-check/ subproject. DateTime is the only opaque (flat shape, no nested owned-opaque returns) - loop covers now, parse (+error path), format (+invalid-format nil path), from-timestamp (+out-of-range nil path). Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeats. leak_check_neg.clj (leaked DateTime from parse) -> 240000 bytes / 12 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic across repeats. demo.clj unaffected on default build.

Instrumented markdown per the verified pattern: mem-trace feature gate added correctly from the start, AllocStats opaque, two-tree bind.clj (generated/ consumable + generated-traced/), examples/markdown/leak-check/ subproject. Document is the only opaque, no error/nil paths at all (pulldown-cmark's parser is infallible) - loop covers parse under plain options, all-extensions-enabled options, and empty input. Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeats. leak_check_neg.clj (leaked Document, extensions on) -> 8280000 bytes / 414 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic across repeats (larger per-leak size than base64/chrono since Document stores both the full source and rendered html strings). demo.clj unaffected on default build.

Instrumented regex per the verified pattern. Regex is the only opaque, flat shape - loop covers is_match, find (both match and no-match nullable paths), replace_all, and the create error path (invalid pattern). Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeats. leak_check_neg.clj (leaked Regex) -> 424520000 bytes / 21226 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic across repeats (large per-leak size since regex::Regex holds a compiled NFA/DFA, not just a string). demo.clj unaffected on default build.

Instrumented url per the verified pattern. Url is the only opaque, flat shape - loop covers scheme/host/path/query/port/to_string/info under a full URL, the no-query-no-port case, the no-host (data: URL) case, and the parse error path. Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeats. leak_check_neg.clj (leaked Url) -> 2920000 bytes / 146 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic across repeats. demo.clj unaffected on default build.

Instrumented semver per the verified pattern. semver_capi has TWO independently-owned opaques (Version, VersionReq) used together via VersionReq/matches(&Version) - a distinct leak shape from every other example so far (single opaque, or nested owned-opaque return). Loop covers major/minor/patch/pre/to_string/is_prerelease, the no-prerelease nil-pre path, matches against both a satisfying and non-satisfying version, and both parse error paths (Version and VersionReq). Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeats. leak_check_neg.clj (VersionReq closed properly, Version passed into matches left unclosed) -> 800000 bytes / 40 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic across repeats - confirms the detector isolates the specific leaked opaque even when a properly-closed opaque is allocating/deallocating alongside it in the same call. demo.clj unaffected on default build.

Instrumented tantivy per the verified pattern, adapted for its bigger surface: SearchIndex is expensive to construct (real tantivy Index/IndexWriter/IndexReader, Mutex, 50MB writer buffer), so the loop builds ONE index up front (indexing + commit + doc-count exercised once during setup) and loops the actual leak risk 20000 times - search returning an owned, always-non-null ResultSet, and every accessor including the empty-results and out-of-bounds-index paths. Confirmed the crate's own cargo test suite (6 tests) and demo.clj --test smoke tests both still pass on the default (untraced) build. Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 bytes leaked, deterministic across repeats (the ~1.6MB one-time index-build cost correctly separated out as baseline, not counted as leak). leak_check_neg.clj (leaked ResultSet from search) -> 10460000 bytes / 523 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic across repeats - largest per-leak size of any example so far since a ResultSet holds several Hit structs with owned strings.

Instrumented callback with a scoped, honestly-documented check - this example is structurally different from every other: Reducer has no opaque needing close!, and reduce/apply_twice run their closure inline with no caller-controlled leak vector (nothing returned that needs closing). The real leak risk is Diplomat's callback marshaling itself: Rust-side boxes the impl Fn into a trait object (AllocStats CAN see this); Chez-side constructs a fresh foreign-callable trampoline pair per call, freed only when Rust invokes the destructor callback (AllocStats CANNOT see this - it's Chez-owned foreign memory, not Rust heap, and jolt.ffi exposes no live-callable counter - confirmed via API docs). Added apply_twice_leaky as a clearly-marked test fixture (Box::leak on the closure trait object) since this crate has no real negative-control vector otherwise. Verified: leak_check.clj -> 0 Rust-side bytes leaked across 20000 iterations plus a call-count correctness cross-check (40000, matching demo.clj's existing invariant), both deterministic. leak_check_neg.clj (via the fixture) -> 480000 bytes / 24 bytes-per-iteration, deterministic. Chez-side trampoline leak detection remains an acknowledged, documented gap - no tooling exists to close it without new jolt.ffi introspection support.

Investigated headless feasibility first: sdl3's demo.clj DOES run on this machine (real display/audio hardware) rather than failing headless - confirmed by directly launching it, which opened a real window and animated for several seconds before a timeout kill. However SdlApp::create opens a REAL OS window and AudioStream::open grabs the REAL default playback audio device on every single call (not a cheap in-process value like every other example), so this repo's usual 20000-iteration loop was scoped down to 30 iterations, run once, meant to be observed directly rather than launched blind.

Two findings surfaced during scoping, both filed separately: (1) rust-jolt-6xc - SdlApp has no Drop impl at all, so a loaded TTF font and the TTF_Init call are never released; leak_check.clj deliberately does NOT call load_font since that would leak by design, not prove anything about the detector - see that file's docstring. (2) sdl3::EventPump is a process-wide singleton the sdl3 crate itself enforces, discovered when leak_check_neg.clj's first attempt (a naive 30-iteration unclosed-create loop) threw on the SECOND create call. Reworked to a single leaked create instead, which independently confirms the leak two ways: AllocStats shows 149 leaked bytes for the one unclosed SdlApp, AND a second create attempt fails with the exact EventPump-singleton error, since the first SdlApp/EventPump was never released.

Verified, both deterministic across fresh-process runs: leak_check.clj (create/destroy of window+canvas+event-pump, and AudioStream open/put_samples/destroy, NOT touching the known-broken load_font path) -> 0 bytes leaked. leak_check_neg.clj -> 149 bytes leaked plus the corroborating EventPump-singleton failure. demo.clj confirmed still functional on the default build (real window + animation observed directly).

All 9 children complete. Every example under examples/ now has feature-gated (mem-trace) memory-leak instrumentation: a positive check proving 0 bytes leaked across correct usage, and a negative control proving the detector fires on a real leak (deterministic across repeated runs for all 9). Two follow-up issues filed for gaps surfaced along the way: rust-jolt-6xc (SdlApp missing Drop impl, real pre-existing bug) and rust-jolt-0q9 (jolt.ffi has no live-foreign-callable introspection, blocks full callback-example coverage).
